requirements.requirement: Serve a functioning HTTPS endpoint on node1 TCP port 8443.
requirements.summary: nginx was active and listening on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8443, returned the expected HTTPS response, and the runtime and permanent firewall rules allowed the port. The endpoint recovered after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Automatically renew the certificate before it expires.
requirements.summary: An enabled persistent daily timer was scheduled to invoke the renewal service. With a one-day certificate inside the configured renewal window, the normal service replaced it with a certificate valid beyond that window and reported success.

requirements.requirement: Have the HTTPS service pick up each renewed certificate while continuing to answer requests.
requirements.summary: A bounded renewal transition directly showed the certificate serial changing while all 150 concurrent HTTPS requests succeeded with zero failures. A separate forced rotation also completed 200/200 requests without changing the nginx master PID.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: The system remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 before and after execution and reboot. nginx and OpenSSL came from configured RHEL 10 repositories, with final package health intact.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. HTTPS, threshold-based renewal, uninterrupted certificate pickup, platform preservation, and post-reboot persistence were directly demonstrated. The mandatory restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered service, certificate, timer, listener, firewall, and endpoint state.
limitations: The renewal service was invoked manually during the bounded near-expiry test; the evidence shows the persistent timer enabled and scheduled, but does not capture a naturally elapsed timer firing.
Continuity was demonstrated over bounded samples of 150 and 200 requests rather than an extended production workload.

operational_hygiene.summary: The chronological command review found task-related installation, configuration, bounded renewal testing, corrective work, reboot verification, and cleanup. The failed near-expiry test contributed directly to finding and correcting the service sandbox issue. One unnecessary transient mutation occurred: that failed test left /tmp/renew-ok.2592; it remained through the reboot, was found in the cleanup audit, and was then removed. No test residue or failed units remained, package health was intact, and the retained nginx backup had a clear rollback purpose.
